peg.nav_basis_note: Theo discloses no thUSD NAV oracle, so the reference is a $1.00 assumption. This deviation is market-vs-par, NOT market-vs-redemption.
peg.market_price_self_referential_basis: The mark is a GeckoTerminal pool price; liquidity.exit_mark is a KyberSwap-routed sell ladder — a different apparatus, so it can contradict the mark. exit_mark.fair_value still borrows this mark, but only to size the rungs in tokens.

sthusd_nav_integrity.note: Quoted convertToAssets vs totalAssets/totalSupply recomputed. Agreement is evidence; divergence would mean the vault's own accounting disagrees with its share price.

liquidity.two_pct_depth_basis: The 200bps crossing is BRACKETED between $100,000 (clears) and $1,000,000 (8,582bps). Published figure is the last rung that cleared, so the true depth sits inside the bracket and above what is shown. Not interpolated -- rung spacing is too coarse to locate it and the curve is not linear across the gap. SLIPPAGE CONVENTION: TOTAL over the fill (not marginal impact at the margin), measured against this venue's own smallest quoted rung. ⚠️ That reference EXCLUDES the smallest rung's own spread, so the figure is price impact and NOT the holder's all-in cost — which is fill_ratio (output_usd / size). Both are real and they answer different questions. The same ladder classifies differently under total vs marginal and under impact vs all-in, so both halves are stated for cross-producer comparison.

liquidity.total_2pct_depth_note: Measured on ONE LEG — the Ethereum KyberSwap sell ladder into USDC (liquidity.exit_mark). Arbitrum is dust and Stable is not reachable by the aggregator, so this is not a cross-chain figure. ⚠️ TVL is not depth: the swept TVL sits almost entirely in one ONE-SIDED Uniswap v4 pool that holds thUSD, not the USDC a seller receives — see exit_mark.quotes for the fill at each size.

exit_mark.slippage_bps_basis: PRICE IMPACT against this venue's own smallest quoted rung, which EXCLUDES that rung's own spread — it is not the holder's all-in cost. The all-in figure is fill_ratio (output_usd / size). Impact is measured this way deliberately, so peg discount and source lag do not leak into it.
exit_mark.scope: ONE LEG: Ethereum only. Arbitrum (~$34K, ~$0 volume) is excluded as dust. Stable holds ~38% of SUPPLY but no indexed DEX venue: GeckoTerminal 404s thUSD there and none of Stable's top 60 pools contain it (2026-10-02; control: GeckoTerminal does index Stable), and KyberSwap does not route Stable. Supply there exits via the bridge, not a pool. Not a cross-chain sum.
exit_mark.fill_ratio_basis: ALL-IN against notional: output_usd / size, where size is converted to tokens at fair_value. Includes the venue's base spread and any gap between fair_value and the venue. 1.0 = exits at fair value; (fill_ratio - 1) * 10000 is the all-in cost in bps.

backing.collateral_ratio_basis: Deliberately null. Total backing is NOT OBSERVABLE: only the on-chain reserve Safe can be read, and >30% of supply is backed off-chain where this repo has no evidence at all. A ratio computed from the observable part would report 42.84% coverage as though it were the whole answer. Use backing.on_chain_coverage_pct, which measures what can actually be seen, and note it is a FRACTION.
backing.collateral_ratio_note: Deliberately null. Total backing is not observable: only the on-chain reserve Safe can be read, and the remainder is off-chain and unverifiable here. Use on_chain_coverage_pct, which measures what can actually be seen.
backing.off_chain_backing_note: RESIDUAL: circulating supply minus on-chain reserves. Ties by construction and is NOT evidence the off-chain backing exists. That >30% of supply lands here is the finding, not a reassurance.

guardrails.by_chain_note: ⚠️ Same timelock address, same Safe address, opposite posture on Ethereum versus Stable and Arbitrum. A delay is only a floor if the Safe CANNOT change it — read safe_holds_timelock_default_admin beside every delay. ⚠️ `timelock_legacy_min_delay_seconds` (64800) is a DIFFERENT CONTRACT (0x46a9ca32) that exists only on Ethereum and is genuinely historical there. Its value coincides with Arbitrum's LIVE delay on 0x2bb4b7e6 — a numeric coincidence between two unrelated contracts, and reading one as the other is the trap this block exists to close.

facts: Elite team and hardened admin chain; unlicensed, non-bankruptcy-remote Panama issuer holding ~57% of backing off-chain and unattested. [riskAnalyst assessment]
Issuer: Theo Network, Panama — unlicensed and NOT bankruptcy-remote. [riskAnalyst assessment]
Credentialed team (ex-Optiver / IMC) with an institutional partner stack — material because thUSD runs an ACTIVE basis trade rather than a passive wrapper. [riskAnalyst assessment]

Material off-chain disclosure gaps: ~57% of supply is backed by assets not observable on-chain; disclosure is via app.theo.xyz/transparency only. [riskAnalyst assessment; the on-chain share is measured here — see backing.on_chain_coverage_pct]

⚠️ Admin config DIFFERS BY CHAIN at the same contract addresses. Ethereum: 48h timelock, 4-of-6 Safe, the Safe's DEFAULT_ADMIN on the timelock revoked. Stable and Arbitrum: 18h timelock, 3-of-5 Safe, and the Safe STILL HOLDS DEFAULT_ADMIN on it — so 18h is a setting that Safe can change, not a floor. Stable carries 99.62% of bridged supply (51,416,246 thUSD) against Arbitrum's 0.38% (195,599), so the weaker configuration governs ~38% of supply-equivalent, not a rounding error. [verified on-chain — Ethereum, Stable and Arbitrum; see asset_specific.guardrails.by_chain]
